lines.text: Can't sleep, and someone told you to try magnesium? Here is what it can do, what it can't, and how to take it safely.
lines.say: Can't sleep, and someone told you to try magnesium? Here is what it can do, what it can't, and how to take it safely.

lines.text: The short answer. Magnesium may help a little, mostly if you are not getting enough of it. It is not a sleeping pill.
lines.say: The short answer. Magnesium may help a little, mostly if you are not getting enough of it. It is not a sleeping pill.

lines.text: Magnesium is a mineral your nerves and muscles depend on. Adults need roughly 300 to 420 milligrams a day, and about half of Americans get less than that from food.
lines.say: Magnesium is a mineral your nerves and muscles depend on. Adults need roughly three hundred to four hundred and twenty milligrams a day, and about half of Americans get less than that from food.

lines.chapter: Why a blood test won't tell you
lines.text: You cannot easily test for it either. Less than 1% of the magnesium in your body is in your blood, so a standard blood test does not show how much you really have.
lines.say: You cannot easily test for it either. Less than one percent of the magnesium in your body is in your blood, so a standard blood test does not show how much you really have.

lines.chapter: Who is more likely to run low
lines.text: Some people are more likely to run low. Older adults, people with type 2 diabetes, people with gut conditions such as Crohn's or coeliac disease, and people who drink heavily. Long-term use of acid-reducing medicines called proton pump inhibitors can lower it too.
lines.say: Some people are more likely to run low. Older adults, people with type two diabetes, people with gut conditions such as Crohn's or coeliac disease, and people who drink heavily. Long-term use of acid-reducing medicines called proton pump inhibitors can lower it too.

lines.text: Why might it help? Magnesium helps regulate the signals that calm the nervous system. That explains the idea. It does not prove a supplement will improve your sleep.
lines.say: Why might it help? Magnesium helps regulate the signals that calm the nervous system. That explains the idea. It does not prove a supplement will improve your sleep.

lines.text: So what do trials show? A review of three trials in older adults with insomnia found people fell asleep about 17 minutes faster on magnesium. But total sleep time did not clearly improve, the trials were small, and the evidence was rated low to very low quality.
lines.say: So what do trials show? A review of three trials in older adults with insomnia found people fell asleep about seventeen minutes faster on magnesium. But total sleep time did not clearly improve, the trials were small, and the evidence was rated low to very low quality.

lines.text: A newer trial gave 155 adults 250 milligrams of magnesium bisglycinate a day. After four weeks, their insomnia scores improved slightly more than with placebo. The effect was small.
lines.say: A newer trial gave one hundred and fifty-five adults two hundred and fifty milligrams of magnesium bisglycinate a day. After four weeks, their insomnia scores improved slightly more than with placebo. The effect was small.

lines.text: The people who improved most were the ones eating the least magnesium. That is an early signal, but it fits: it is most likely to help if you are running low.
lines.say: The people who improved most were the ones eating the least magnesium. That is an early signal, but it fits: it is most likely to help if you are running low.

lines.text: Which form? Ones that dissolve well, like citrate, are absorbed better than oxide. Glycinate is the form that newer trial used. Oxide, carbonate, chloride and gluconate are the ones most likely to cause diarrhoea.
lines.say: Which form? Ones that dissolve well, like citrate, are absorbed better than oxide. Glycinate is the form that newer trial used. Oxide, carbonate, chloride and gluconate are the ones most likely to cause diarrhoea.

lines.text: You will also see special forms sold for sleep. No form has been shown to beat the others for sleep in head-to-head trials.
lines.say: You will also see special forms sold for sleep. No form has been shown to beat the others for sleep in head-to-head trials.

lines.text: How much? For adults, the upper limit for magnesium from supplements is 350 milligrams a day. Check the label for elemental magnesium, not the weight of the whole compound.
lines.say: How much? For adults, the upper limit for magnesium from supplements is three hundred and fifty milligrams a day. Check the label for elemental magnesium, not the weight of the whole compound.

lines.text: Too much causes diarrhoea, nausea and stomach cramps. If that happens, lower the dose or change the form.
lines.say: Too much causes diarrhoea, nausea and stomach cramps. If that happens, lower the dose or change the form.

lines.text: That is no accident. Magnesium is the active ingredient in some laxatives. One tablespoon of milk of magnesia contains 500 milligrams, well over the supplement limit.
lines.say: That is no accident. Magnesium is the active ingredient in some laxatives. One tablespoon of milk of magnesia contains five hundred milligrams, well over the supplement limit.

lines.text: Food counts too, and magnesium from food has no upper limit. An ounce of pumpkin seeds has about 156 milligrams. An ounce of almonds, 80. Half a cup of cooked spinach, 78. Black beans, brown rice and yogurt all add more.
lines.say: Food counts too, and magnesium from food has no upper limit. An ounce of pumpkin seeds has about one hundred and fifty-six milligrams. An ounce of almonds, eighty. Half a cup of cooked spinach, seventy-eight. Black beans, brown rice and yogurt all add more.

lines.text: Refining grains strips out much of the magnesium, so whole grains beat white bread and white rice. And your body absorbs only 30 to 40% of what you eat.
lines.say: Refining grains strips out much of the magnesium, so whole grains beat white bread and white rice. And your body absorbs only thirty to forty percent of what you eat.

lines.text: Who should check first? Anyone with kidney disease, because the kidneys clear extra magnesium. It can also stop some antibiotics and osteoporosis medicines being absorbed, so take them at least two hours apart and ask a pharmacist. Some water tablets change magnesium levels as well.
lines.say: Who should check first? Anyone with kidney disease, because the kidneys clear extra magnesium. It can also stop some antibiotics and osteoporosis medicines being absorbed, so take them at least two hours apart and ask a pharmacist. Some water tablets change magnesium levels as well.

lines.text: If you have slept badly for more than three months, see a doctor. Long-term insomnia has proven treatments, and a supplement should not delay them.
lines.say: If you have slept badly for more than three months, see a doctor. Long-term insomnia has proven treatments, and a supplement should not delay them.

lines.text: And the basics still matter more: a regular sleep window, less caffeine late in the day, and a dark, cool room.
lines.say: And the basics still matter more: a regular sleep window, less caffeine late in the day, and a dark, cool room.

lines.text: So. Magnesium is cheap, and worth a try if your diet is low in it. Expect a small effect, stay under 350 milligrams from supplements, and judge it after four weeks. Sources are in the description. This is general information, not medical advice.
lines.say: So. Magnesium is cheap, and worth a try if your diet is low in it. Expect a small effect, stay under three hundred and fifty milligrams from supplements, and judge it after four weeks. Sources are in the description. This is general information, not medical advice.
